_why: What the built workbench is allowed to cost, in bytes, gzipped. `npm run check:weight` measures `dist/assets/**` plus `dist/index.html` after `npm run build` and fails when a metric is over its number or has nothing measured behind it. It also refuses a build older than its own sources (exit 2, naming the newer files, `--allow-stale` to override), because Run 165 quoted 950.3 kB measured from a `dist/` built before the features it was verifying. The budgets are hand-edited, deliberately: raise one with the reason in the commit, never by recording first. `entry_gzip` is what a first paint waits for — the document, its module script, the chunks it preloads and its stylesheets — and it is the number both splits moved: 627.5 kB in one chunk, 585.5 kB once the ten tabs became lazy chunks, **432.9 kB** once CodeMirror left the preload list too (the editor is a `React.lazy` boundary inside the runner, so the code, the Run button and the lesson text paint before the editor is parsed). Its budget came down to 470 kB for that reason: a static `@codemirror` import, or a tab folded back into the entry, fails here (Run 177 confirmed it: a statically imported Vim package pulled 149 kB of CodeMirror back into the entry's preloads, and the split into `vendor-vim` with a dynamic import put the entry back to 446 kB). `largest_js_gzip` was 614 kB when the app was one chunk and is 263 kB now, so its budget is 300 kB; the editor's own chunk (148.6 kB) is not the entry's problem any more but it still has to fit. `fonts` counts the woff2 files as they are (woff2 is already compressed, and every unicode-range subset is emitted — a Latin learner fetches roughly 140 kB of the 302 kB). `total` is a ceiling on the bundle as a whole, not the cost of a visit: the lazy chunks are all emitted whether or not a learner opens their tabs. `js_gzip` moved to 700 kB for the Vim keymap (`vendor-vim`, 39 kB): the chunk is fetched only when the keys are turned on — which is what keeps `entry_gzip` where it is — but this metric counts every emitted byte, so the ceiling has to know about it. **It moved to 720 kB for the debugger's last two pieces** (Run 188–189): watch expressions (a field, a chip row and a store in the runner chunk) and the Black formatter (a toolbar button, a status line, a palette command and the request method). Both are app code, not libraries — Black is fetched into Pyodide at the first Format press and ships in no chunk at all — so the only way to keep them out of this metric would be to split the runner itself, which would cost the learner an extra round trip on the tab that opens first. 700 kB was 381 B short of the measured 700.4; 720 kB leaves 19.6 kB of headroom for the next piece rather than a budget that fails on the following button. `total` moved with it, to 1.04 MB: it is the sum of the emitted bytes, so raising one metric without the ceiling would have moved the failure to a number nobody edited — it was 1.1 kB short after the same two pieces, which is a budget that cannot take a third. **`prose_gzip` is new with Run 193**: the searchable text of the 65 reading pages (`dist/prose-index.json`, written by `scripts/generate_prose_index.py`) is fetched only the first time `⌘⇧F` is opened, so it is neither JavaScript nor part of the shell and is measured on its own — 206.6 kB measured against a 220 kB ceiling, with the ~13 kB of room a page or two of new prose can use before the number moves deliberately. It is not in `total` for the same reason it is not in `entry_gzip`: a learner who never searches should not be charged for it in a report about what a visit costs. **Four ceilings moved for Runs 196–197**, by hand and 10 kB at a time: the help sheet (a report builder, a modal and the runner's assembly of its input) and the pair session (a protocol module, a WebRTC hook and a second modal) are app code on the first-screen chunk — the runner is the tab this app opens on, so a `React.lazy` boundary there would only add a fetch before the lesson appears, which is the trade `entry_gzip` exists to avoid. Measured: entry 464.5 → 468.8 kB, js 712.8 → 717.1, largest 292.6 → 296.6, total 1.03 → 1.04 MB. The old ceilings would have left 1.2 kB of entry and 2.9 kB of js — a budget that fails on the next control rather than on a regression — so `entry_gzip` is 480 kB, `js_gzip` 735 kB, `largest_js_gzip` 305 kB and `total` 1.06 MB: room for one more small feature, not for a library. **Run 198's co-editing spent that room, not a new ceiling**: the character CRDT, its diff and the sheet's co-edit block are app code in the same runner chunk, measured at entry 468.8 → 472.0 kB, js 717.1 → 720.5, largest 296.6 → 299.9, total 1.04 MB — still 8 kB inside the entry's number, so nothing moved by hand this time, and the record was refreshed. **A twelfth tab moved two ceilings (Run 202).** The Board tab runs compiled firmware: `avr8js` (9.3 kB gzipped, its own `vendor-avr` chunk — the catch-all `vendor` chunk is preloaded, so leaving the emulator in it put 9.6 kB in every first visit for a tab nobody opened, and `entry_gzip` caught it at 481.7 kB before the split), the tab's own 3.7 kB, and `avrSim` 1.25 kB. None of it is on the first paint: `entry_gzip` measured 472.4 kB against its unchanged 480 kB, which is the split doing its job. `js_gzip` is 740.5 → 750 kB and `total` 1.06 → 1.08 MB, because this metric counts every emitted byte and the tab's chunk is emitted whether or not it is opened; the ~9.5 kB of room is one more small feature, not a library. **Both shapes are budgeted (Run 207)**: `budgets` below is the local-only build — no Supabase variables, so the account branch folds away and its chunk is a one-byte stub — and `signed_in` carries the two ceilings the CI build's extra bytes need; the gate names the shape it measured, and the record's `variant` says which one the `measured` block describes. **The shipped shape is graded on every run (Run 226)**: when `dist/` is the local-only build, `npm run check:weight` builds the signed-in one into `dist-signed-in/` with placeholder Supabase values, measures it against the `signed_in` ceilings, and removes it — the Run 207 breach was invisible locally because the gate had only ever seen the local-only bundle; CI's `dist/` is already signed-in, so it builds nothing extra. **The reader moved four ceilings, by hand (Run 229).** The lesson text beside the editor (`app/src/components/LessonReader.tsx`, its payload loader and its inline parser) is app code on the first-screen chunk, because the runner is the tab the app opens on and a lazy boundary there would put a fetch before the lesson appears. Measured: entry 474.3 → 479.4 kB local and 475.1 → 481.4 signed-in, js 741.2 → 747.1 and 801.0 → 807.0, largest 300.8 → 306.7, total 1.0602 → 1.0665 MB and 1.12 → 1.1264 MB. The old numbers had 1.5 kB of entry left and no room in `largest_js_gzip` at all, so they are raised to 495 kB entry, 765 kB js local and 825 kB signed-in, 320 kB largest and 1.10/1.16 MB total: room for one more small feature, not a library. **`reader_gzip` is new with the same run**: the generated payloads under `dist/lesson-pages/**` (92 pages, one per registry entry, written by `scripts/generate_lesson_pages.py`) are served beside the bundle and fetched one page at a time when a lesson opens, so like `prose_gzip` they are neither JavaScript nor part of a first paint and are not in `total`. 669.2 kB measured against a 720 kB ceiling — about seven pages of new prose before the number moves deliberately. **The account release moved six ceilings, by hand.** The optional account flow added three lazy screens (the account panel at 4.1 kB gzipped, the learner dashboard and the admin area), plus the workspace merge/sync modules and the public-settings reader on the first-screen chunk. Measured before the move: entry 479.4 → 485.1 kB local and 481.4 → 487.1 signed-in, js 747.1 → 762.6 and 807.0 → 822.4, largest 306.7 → 311.7, total 1.0665 → 1.08 MB and 1.1264 → 1.14 MB. The old ceilings had 2.4 kB and 2.6 kB of js left — a budget that fails on the next control rather than on a regression — so they are 505 kB entry, 790 kB js local and 850 kB signed-in, 325 kB largest, 1.13/1.19 MB total. The three screens are `React.lazy` boundaries: a visitor who never signs in does not download them, and a first paint that grows by the whole account UI would still fail this gate. **Maths became self-hosted, and moved three ceilings (Run 239).** The formulas used to borrow a jsdelivr copy of `katex.min.css` — pinned to 0.16.21 while the JavaScript came from the installed 0.16.47 — so a page with an equation depended on a third-party host and on a version nobody had tested. The stylesheet is now imported from the package (`app/src/main.tsx`) and its faces are emitted into `dist/assets/` (woff2 only: `vite.config.ts` drops the `woff`/`ttf` sources, which would have added 1.17 MB of files no current browser asks for). Measured: fonts 302.7 → **558.9 kB** (19 KaTeX faces, 256.2 kB of woff2), css 14.7 → 22.2 kB (+7.5 kB of KaTeX rules and `@font-face` declarations), total 1.08 → **1.35 MB** local and 1.14 → **1.41 MB** signed-in. `entry_gzip` moved only by the stylesheet link (485.1 → 492.8 kB local, 481.4 → 494.8 signed-in) and keeps its 505 kB ceiling with 12 kB left: the KaTeX JavaScript chunk was already preloaded, because `MathView` is statically reachable. The fonts are emitted weight, not visit weight — a browser downloads a face only when a rendered glyph needs it, so a page of plain `$x$` fetches Main-Regular (26 kB) and nothing else — but `fonts` counts every emitted file, which is the honest number for a bundle that has to carry them offline. Ceilings are 600 kB fonts, 26 kB css, 1.40/1.46 MB total: room for one more small feature, not another font family.

signed_in._why: The same source builds a bigger bundle when the Supabase variables are set, which is how CI builds it (the anon key is a repository variable; the build is local-only on a fresh clone). Run 207 is why this block exists. CI's `entry_gzip` read 532.6 kB against the 480 kB ceiling — a real breach nobody saw locally — because `@supabase/supabase-js` was being parked by the catch-all in the statically preloaded `vendor` chunk. The fix is a split, not a ceiling: `vite.config.ts` sends it to its own `vendor-auth` chunk, which the account panel fetches when it opens, so `entry_gzip` measured 475.1 kB with accounts configured and needs no override — and it should not get one, because a first paint that differs between the two shapes would mean the split regressed. What the library really costs is emitted bytes: 57.8 kB gzipped in `vendor-auth` plus the account panel's own code in the runner chunk. (Both builds emit a `vendor-auth` file; without the variables it is the one-byte stub the folded-away import leaves, which is why the gate tells the shapes apart by that chunk's raw size rather than by its name.) `js_gzip` 801.0 kB measured against 810 kB (9 kB of room) and `total` 1.12 MB against 1.14 MB (20 kB), both by hand and by this measurement. The other five metrics are the same file in both shapes and keep their base ceilings, so a font or a stylesheet cannot grow just because someone built with a key.
